allowable_costs:
EMPG funds support efforts to build and sustain core capabilities across all mission areas — Prevention, Protection, Mitigation, Response, and Recovery .
These broad categories include:
- Personnel — salaries and benefits for emergency management staff whose work supports preparedness and program implementation.
- Planning — development, review, and revision of EOPs, hazard mitigation plans, continuity plans, and related preparedness documents.
- Training — delivery and participation in emergency management and NIMS/ICS training.
- Exercises — design, conduct, evaluation, and improvement planning for exercises.
- Equipment — limited to items that directly support emergency management operations and preparedness (not response‑only equipment).
- Operational costs — communications systems, EOC operations, public preparedness outreach, and program administration.
title: FY2026 EMPG
eligibility_criteria:
At the local level, states typically require municipalities to meet specific operational and compliance standards to receive EMPG pass‑through funding. For example, Connecticut’s state-level criteria (representative of common requirements nationally) include:
- Officially appointed Emergency Management Director (EMD).
- Current Local Emergency Operations Plan (LEOP) updated every two years and signed by the EMD and Chief Executive Officer.
- Participation in statewide communication systems, such as high‑band radio networks and quarterly radio tests.
- Active use of WebEOC for situational awareness and reporting.
- 24/7 contact information provided to the state regional coordinator.
- Participation in required statewide exercises, such as annual EPPI exercises.
